From the world to the two retinas

Reading the map

Every point in space belongs to the left half of the world or the right, and each half lands on the nasal retina of one eye and the temporal retina of the other. Those two sheets meet at the chiasm and travel together from there — which is why a lesion behind the chiasm never respects the boundary between the eyes.

The far edges of each half-field (A and D) are the monocular crescents: the nose blocks them from the other eye. Blind one optic nerve and that crescent is gone outright, even though the rest of the field is still covered.
